To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transcriptomes of stromal cells that support HSPCs are differentially expressed depending on the O2 concentration, and that the expression of several genes and pathways that regulate HSPCs, such as Wnts and Angiopoietins, are differentially regulated by the O2 concentration.

the stromal cells produce different ECMs that are able to support expansion of different HSPCs and the transcriptome profiling of stromal cells that support expansion of different types of HSPCs has revealed the differential expression of known niche factors and several novel genes.

the gene expression profiles of matrices prepared from stromal cell cultures under different oxygen tensions and in the presence of different culture conditions are significantly different and can provide a better understanding of the complex network of signals that regulate hematopoiesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of genes and pathways that are involved in the support of hematopoietics stem/progenitor cell functions.
the development of an efficient ex vivo culture system for the expansion of human HSPCs, which will provide a source of HSCs for transplantation.
the identification of novel genes that regulate HSPC self-renewal, expansion and differentiation in the hematopoietics niche.
